newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in Europe, edge higher in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in Europe, edge higher in Hong Kong.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Leading blue chips stumbled from record levels set last week amid concerns about monetary policy on both sides of the Atlantic. The FTSE 100 closed 44.4 points lower at 3,919.7, after climbing to a record 3,994.1 on Friday. Losses were broadbased, with decliners beating advancers by a margin of nine to one.

FRANKFURT - Stocks closed sharply lower amid profit-taking after recent rallies and continuing uncertainty ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday. The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 19.06 points at 2,627.04. In late electronic trade, the IBIS DAX index closed further down at 2,624.18.

PARIS - Stocks closed lower along with other markets, among which was an early 50-point fall in the Dow Jones industrial average, on fears that the Fed will raise U.S. rates on Tuesday. The French fall was also due to profit-taking on the last day of the September account. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 12.37 points at 2,067.09.

ZURICH - Stocks followed weak European bourses to close slightly off the day's lows due to insecurity ahead of Tuesday's Fed meeting and a fall in Swiss index heavyweights Ciba, Sandoz, Roche and Nestle. The all-share SPI gave up 34.13 points, or 1.44 percent, to 2,334.28 points.
TOKYO - The stock market was closed for a national holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday. On Friday, the key 225-issue Nikkei average closed down 210.61 points or 0.99 percent at 21,112.24.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended firm, after the Hang Seng index hit a new 1996 intra-day high, with investors hoping that if the U.S. Federal Reserve raises interest rates this week, it will only be a small hike. The Hang Seng index closed the session 29.77 points higher at 11,622.13, after hitting a year high at 11,684.00.

SYDNEY - The stock market dived to its lowest closing level in six weeks on continuing concern on the future of base metal prices. The All Ordinaries index fell 21.6 points to 2219.20. With offshore markets regularly reaching record highs, local traders expressed dismay at the local market's lacklutre performance.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended weak in listless trade, with industrials easing amid a lack of interest and golds depressed by a softer bullion price. Dealers said the market had almost ground to a standstill in the afternoon ahead of the Heritage Day public holiday on Tuesday and on the Jewish Yom Kippur holiday today. The overall index shed 17.4 points to 6,917.9 points. The Industrial index was down 19.9 points to 8,170.9 points and gold index fell 16.5 points to 1,721.4 points.
